Collision Report — i2m Futures Innovation
Section 0 — Challenge Framing
Job-to-be-Done
When industrial operators rely on filtration-critical processes, they want predictable filtration performance with minimal energy use and maintenance attention, so they can protect uptime, quality and operating cost without constantly managing the filtration system.
Top 3 Pains
  • Reactive, maintenance-heavy filtration.
  • Energy cost is disconnected from customer economics.
  • Customers buy hardware but still carry performance risk.
Top 3 Gains
  • Predictable performance.
  • Lower total energy and maintenance burden.
  • A supplier accountable for measurable outcomes.
Section 1 — Expert Panel Selected
The panel deliberately collides climate urgency, nature-based design, regenerative systems, development, free-market economics, affordability and energy-abundance perspectives. The objective is productive tension, not consensus.
Ani Dasgupta
H6 · President & CEO, World Resources Institute
Systems-oriented climate and development leader who views environmental action as inseparable from economic development, urban transformation, equity and human well-being. Connects local interventions to institutional scale, governance, finance, inclusion and implementation capacity.
Bold Idea
Build a cross-sector transition model that links climate benefit to affordability, governance and quality-of-life outcomes.
Provocation
Can this become scalable, equitable infrastructure rather than another impressive pilot?
Kate Orff
H7 · Landscape architect · Founder, SCAPE
Treats landscapes as active infrastructure and favors ecological, adaptive and place-specific solutions that protect people while restoring natural systems. Looks for hybrid blue-green infrastructure, biodiversity, community value and resilience rather than isolated hard-engineering fixes.
Bold Idea
Replace a single-purpose engineered intervention with a hybrid living system that protects, adapts and regenerates.
Provocation
Why solve one technical problem if the intervention could also restore ecology and strengthen communities?
Greta Thunberg
H8 · Climate activist · Fridays for Future
Evaluates proposals through measurable climate impact, ecological limits and intergenerational responsibility rather than corporate narratives or incremental improvement. Looks for real emissions reduction, speed, scientific alignment and evidence of greenwashing or delayed action.
Bold Idea
Define a hard science-based impact threshold and reject concepts that cannot demonstrate material change within the required timeframe.
Provocation
Does this reduce the problem at the speed and scale science requires — or make continued inaction easier to justify?
William McDonough
H9 · Architect · Cradle-to-Cradle pioneer
Moves beyond “less bad” sustainability toward regenerative systems where materials are designed for continuous biological or technical cycles. Treats waste, toxicity and disposability as design failures and asks what every material becomes next.
Bold Idea
Redesign the concept so every material and output has a safe next cycle and the system becomes regenerative by design.
Provocation
Why minimize the footprint when the system could be designed to create a positive one?
Julian Simon
H10 · Economist · Counter-Malthusian thinker
Views human ingenuity, knowledge, markets and technological substitution as the ultimate resource capable of turning scarcity into innovation and abundance. Looks for price signals, entrepreneurship, substitution, discovery and unintended consequences of restricting growth.
Bold Idea
Use scarcity signals to create an open innovation challenge that rewards substitution, efficiency and unexpected alternatives.
Provocation
Are we treating people as consumers of scarce resources — or as the creators of new resources and solutions?
Diana Furchtgott-Roth
H11 · Economist · Free-market policy advocate
Starts from affordability, reliability, resilience and economic competitiveness and is skeptical of mandates that impose large costs without demonstrated benefits. Stress-tests full economic cost, energy prices, industrial competitiveness, consumer choice and dependence on subsidies or regulation.
Bold Idea
Design the offer so its economics survive without subsidy: transparent total cost, reliability and voluntary customer adoption.
Provocation
Would customers voluntarily choose this at scale, or does the business case only work because policy forces adoption?
Michael Shellenberger
H12 · Author · Environmental commentator
Combines environmental concern with advocacy for nuclear power, energy abundance, technological modernization and economic development. Looks for energy density, reliability, scalability and human welfare while challenging symbolic or high-cost climate policies.
Bold Idea
Pair environmental ambition with dense, reliable energy and technology that can scale without constraining human development.
Provocation
Does this green solution improve energy, emissions and human welfare at scale — or mainly satisfy a narrative?
Section 2 — The Collision Meeting
Greta Thunberg → responding to Diana Furchtgott-Roth
“Affordability cannot become an excuse for solutions whose climate impact is too small or too late.”
Diana Furchtgott-Roth → responding to Greta Thunberg
“And urgency cannot erase economics. If households and industry cannot afford the transition, it will not survive at scale.”
Kate Orff → responding to Michael Shellenberger
“Energy abundance is not the whole system. Infrastructure can protect people while rebuilding ecological capacity instead of consuming more of it.”
Julian Simon → responding to Kate Orff and Greta Thunberg
“Scarcity is also information. Give people incentives and freedom to invent substitutes before assuming limits require restriction.”
William McDonough → responding to Julian Simon
“Ingenuity matters, but design intention matters too. Innovation that produces permanent waste is simply incomplete design.”
Ani Dasgupta → responding to the room
“The winning concept has to survive all of these tests at once: climate, people, nature, economics, institutions and implementation.”
Collision Combinations
⚡ Regenerative Abundance
Fuse McDonough’s regenerative design with Simon’s ingenuity thesis: design scarcity out through materials that circulate continuously and markets that reward better substitutes.
⚡ Nature + Nuclear Resilience
Combine Orff’s ecological infrastructure with Shellenberger’s energy-abundance logic: resilient systems that use nature where it performs best and dense reliable technology where it matters most.
⚡ Climate Impact Without the Mandate
Force Thunberg’s science-based impact threshold through Furchtgott-Roth’s affordability test: a solution radical enough to matter, but attractive enough that customers choose it without coercion.
Section 3 — The Final Concept
Regenerative Resilience Platform
A filtration-as-an-outcome service combining physical filtration expertise, minimal sensing and adaptive decision logic to guarantee one measurable result — such as energy use, air quality, water recovery or uptime — while hiding technical complexity from the operator and proving full-system economics before scale-up.
Why It Is Non-Obvious
The concept is neither “smart filtration” nor a service contract. It emerges from forcing technology optimism, human-centered simplicity, physical constraints and market experimentation into one proposition where MANN+HUMMEL takes responsibility for the customer outcome.
3 First Experiment Steps (≤ 6 weeks, low budget)
  1. Interview five target customers and quantify one costly filtration outcome in € / energy / downtime / risk.
  2. Build the smallest closed-loop demonstrator linking one sensor signal, one filtration parameter and one customer KPI.
  3. Offer three customers a low-risk pilot framed around a guaranteed KPI and record willingness to pay, objections and proof requirements.
